cards.back: A whole number. It can be positive, negative or zero. Examples: -3, 0, 12.
cards.say: integer. A whole number. It can be positive, negative or zero. Examples: negative three, zero, twelve.

cards.back: A small raised number that shows how many times to multiply a number by itself. In 2³ the index is 3.
cards.say: index, power. A small raised number that shows how many times to multiply a number by itself. In two to the power of three, the index is three.

cards.back: A number that gives the original number when multiplied by itself. The square root of 49 is 7.
cards.say: square root. A number that gives the original number when multiplied by itself. The square root of forty nine is seven.

cards.back: The number that is multiplied by itself three times to give the original number. The cube root of 8 is 2, because 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
cards.say: cube root. The number that is multiplied by itself three times to give the original number. The cube root of eight is two, because two times two times two equals eight.

cards.back: A factor that is also a prime number. The prime factors of 12 are 2 and 3.
cards.say: prime factor. A factor that is also a prime number. The prime factors of twelve are two and three.

cards.back: The biggest number that is a factor of two or more numbers. The HCF of 12 and 18 is 6.
cards.say: highest common factor, HCF. The biggest number that is a factor of two or more numbers. The HCF of twelve and eighteen is six.

cards.back: The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. The LCM of 4 and 6 is 12.
cards.say: lowest common multiple, LCM. The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. The LCM of four and six is twelve.

cards.back: Numbers, letters and operations written together, with no equals sign. Example: 3n + 2.
cards.say: expression. Numbers, letters and operations written together, with no equals sign. Example: three n plus two.

cards.back: A statement with an equals sign that is true for certain values. Example: n + 4 = 9.
cards.say: equation. A statement with an equals sign that is true for certain values. Example: n plus four equals nine.

cards.back: A rule written with letters. Example: area of a rectangle = length × width.
cards.say: formula. A rule written with letters. Example: area of a rectangle equals length times width.

cards.back: The operation that undoes another one. Subtraction is the inverse of addition.
cards.say: inverse operation. The operation that undoes another one. Subtraction is the inverse of addition.

cards.back: A number out of 100. 40% means 40 out of 100.
cards.say: percentage. A number out of one hundred. Forty percent means forty out of one hundred.

cards.back: Compares amounts of different things. 2:3 means 2 parts to 3 parts.
cards.say: ratio. Compares amounts of different things. Two to three means two parts to three parts.

cards.back: A number from 0 to 1 that shows how likely an event is.
cards.say: probability. A number from zero to one that shows how likely an event is.

cards.back: Sliding a shape without turning or flipping it.
cards.say: translation. Sliding a shape without turning or flipping it.

cards.back: Flipping a shape over a mirror line so it makes a mirror image.
cards.say: reflection. Flipping a shape over a mirror line so it makes a mirror image.

cards.back: Turning a shape about a point through a certain angle.
cards.say: rotation. Turning a shape about a point through a certain angle.

cards.back: One of the four regions on a coordinate grid, made by the x-axis and y-axis.
cards.say: quadrant. One of the four regions on a coordinate grid, made by the x axis and y axis.

cards.back: The height of a shape measured at a right angle to its base.
cards.say: perpendicular height. The height of a shape measured at a right angle to its base.
